block_mixture_closure.status: COMPLETE ANALYTICAL CONDITIONAL CLOSURE; NOT A UNIVERSAL PAIR-TABLE THEOREM
block_mixture_closure.statement: Let G be a finite simple graph with n vertices, m edges, c connected components and beta=m-n+c. Partition the alphabet into disjoint nonempty classes Omega_i with positive masses pi_i summing to1. Let kappa_i be positive probabilities on Omega_i and lambda_i symmetric pair laws with marginals kappa_i. Suppose on each actual connected component C there exists a law tau_i,C with every singleton kappa_i, every edge lambda_i, and D(tau_i,C||kappa_i^V(C))<=|E(C)| I_i, where I_i=D(lambda_i||kappa_i^2). Define kappa(x)=pi_i kappa_i(x) on Omega_i and lambda(x,y)=pi_i lambda_i(x,y) if x,y belong to the same class, and0 otherwise. Then an actual-vertex witness tau_0 has every singleton kappa, every edge lambda, and D(tau_0||kappa^V)<=mD(lambda||kappa^2)-beta H(pi). Natural logarithms are used; H(pi)=-sum_i pi_i log pi_i.
proof: Independently for each connected component C, choose one block label i with probability pi_i, then sample tau_i,C on its actual vertices. Distinct blocks have disjoint supports, so this specifies a probability without ambiguous overlapping latent encodings. Its singleton and every individual actual-edge table are exactly the stated kappa and lambda.

On a component with n_C vertices, the likelihood ratio of a block-i configuration is pi_i tau_i,C(x)/(pi_i^n_C kappa_i^V(C)(x)). Averaging its logarithm gives D_C=(n_C-1)H(pi)+sum_i pi_i D(tau_i,C||kappa_i^V(C)). Isolated vertices have n_C=1 and zero cost.

The pair-level likelihood ratio is pi_i lambda_i/(pi_i^2 kappa_i^2), so I=D(lambda||kappa^2)=H(pi)+sum_i pi_i I_i. Summing the component formula and the assumed component bounds yields D(tau_0||kappa^V)<=(n-c)H(pi)+m sum_i pi_i I_i=mI-beta H(pi). The empty graph has n=m=c=0 and the same zero identity. No approximation, global triple-orbit mixing, or assumed independence of actual edge constraints appears.
block_mixture_closure.triple_extension: If each lambda_i is the pair marginal of an exchangeable eta_i, then eta=sum_i pi_i eta_i on the disjoint blocks is an exchangeable triple extension of lambda. Thus the closure respects the original restricted input cone, but the entropy identity itself does not require this extension.
block_mixture_closure.limit: This handles block-diagonal input tables with separately available exact within-block witnesses. It does not imply every triple-extendible table has such a partition or that arbitrary shared triple-orbit mixtures preserve a sharp bound.

global_IID_noise_budget_transfer.statement: For any exact witness tau_0 with singleton kappa, pair lambda_0 and slack Delta=mD(lambda_0||kappa^2)-D(tau_0||kappa^V), set lambda_epsilon=(1-epsilon)lambda_0+epsilon kappa^2 and nu=(1-epsilon)tau_0+epsilon kappa^V,0<=epsilon<=1. Then nu has every target marginal exactly and mD(lambda_epsilon||kappa^2)-D(nu||kappa^V)>=(1-epsilon)Delta-m h(epsilon), with h(t)=-t log t-(1-t)log(1-t).
global_IID_noise_budget_transfer.proof: Convexity gives D(nu||kappa^V)<=(1-epsilon)D(tau_0||kappa^V). Introduce the Bernoulli mixture label at the pair level. The chain rule gives (1-epsilon)D(lambda_0||kappa^2)=D(lambda_epsilon||kappa^2)+I(label;pair); its mutual information is at most h(epsilon). Subtract the two bounds. This is one global joint mixture, so label entropy can be paid from existing cycle slack; unlike arbitrary orbit mixtures it does not claim a sharp bound when Delta=0.

buffered_full_table_perturbation.status: COMPLETE EXPLICIT ANALYTICAL LEMMA; FIXED FINITE GRAPH, NOT A GLOBAL ARBITRARY-TABLE COVERAGE THEOREM
buffered_full_table_perturbation.statement: Let G be a finite simple graph with n>=2 vertices and m>=1 edges, q>=2 colors and fixed positive singleton kappa. Write a=min kappa,b=max kappa. Suppose tau_0 has exact kappa/lambda_0 marginals and entropy slack Delta=mD(lambda_0||kappa^2)-D(tau_0||kappa^V)>0. Choose0<epsilon<1 and set nu=(1-epsilon)tau_0+epsilon R, R=kappa^V,lambda_epsilon=(1-epsilon)lambda_0+epsilon kappa^2. Let D be any symmetric row-zero table, g(x,y)=Dxy/(kappa_x kappa_y),gamma=max|g| and d=(1/2)sum|D|. If m gamma<=epsilon,d<=1-q^(-2),and m d<=1-q^(-n), define tau=nu+R sum_e g(x_u,x_v). Then tau is an exact probability with all singleton kappa and every edge lambda_epsilon+D. It has budget slack at least (1-epsilon)Delta-m h(epsilon)-m E_2(d)-E_n(m d), where E_j(t)=h(t)+t log(q^j-1)+j t log(b/a). In particular every D satisfying these conditions and a positive right side meets the sharp target.
proof: The density of nu relative to R is at least epsilon. The signed correction density is at least-m gamma, so tau>=0. Row-zero means sum_y kappa_y g(x,y)=0. On a finite simple graph, integration of any correction except the same actual edge kills at least one centered endpoint; hence its total and singleton integrals vanish and every actual edge correction is exactly D. Simplicity rules out a second edge with the same endpoint pair. Thus normalization and every full edge law are exact.

Triangle inequality gives TV(tau,nu)<=(m/2)E_{kappa^2}|g|=m d. The pair distance is d. Both stated TV thresholds are imposed separately: the joint threshold need not imply the pair threshold when a graph has isolated vertices. In the small neighborhood conclusion below both bounds automatically hold.

For laws P,Q with fixed positive reference R_j=kappa^j and TV t<=1-q^(-j), maximal-coupling entropy continuity gives |H(P)-H(Q)|<=h(t)+t log(q^j-1). The difference of expectations of log R_j is at most t times its range, j log(b/a). Therefore |D(P||R_j)-D(Q||R_j)|<=E_j(t). E_j is increasing on the stated interval, because h(t)+t log(q^j-1) is and the added linear term is nonnegative. Apply it to the pair with d and to the joint with upper bound m d. Combine with the preceding global mixture bound.

Choose epsilon small enough that (1-epsilon)Delta-m h(epsilon)>0, possible since h(epsilon)->0. Then choose sufficiently small D: gamma and d tend to zero in the finite table space, so positivity and both TV thresholds hold, while both continuity losses tend to zero. This gives an explicit non-IFT full-dimensional relative neighborhood of compatible pair tables around lambda_epsilon for fixed kappa. Its size depends on the actual graph and base slack; it is not uniform over all subdivision path lengths.

If lambda_0 admits an exchangeable eta_0, the mixed eta_epsilon=(1-epsilon)eta_0+epsilon kappa^3 is positive. The correction eta=eta_epsilon+kappa_x kappa_y kappa_z(g(x,y)+g(x,z)+g(y,z)) changes its pair by exactly D and preserves exchangeability/singletons. It stays nonnegative when3 gamma<=epsilon, and strictly positive when3 gamma<epsilon. In a bipartite K4 subdivision m>=8, the stronger strict buffer condition m gamma<epsilon implies this, so the produced neighborhood can stay within the positive triple-extendible input cone.
buffered_full_table_perturbation.qualification: The displayed lemma is used with BOTH TV conditions d<=1-q^(-2) and m d<=1-q^(-n). These are explicit, not inferred from the second condition for a graph with isolated vertices. This lemma supplies budget transfer only near a known strict-slack witness, not an arbitrary source of slack for every triple input.

construction_and_proof.step: 1. A block boundary law and its actual within-block witness
construction_and_proof.argument: Set lambda_0=[[1/3,0,0],[0,1/9,2/9],[0,2/9,1/9]]. It splits into block{1} of mass1/3 and block{2,3} of mass2/3. In the second block, the conditional singleton is uniform binary and the conditional pair has diagonal1/6 and offdiagonal1/3, agreement s=1/3. The previously fully source-reviewed uniform binary Potts theorem on this actual bipartite subcubic G supplies a joint tau_B with every edge this exact pair, D(tau_B||uniform_binary^V)<=m I_B, and a Gibbs representation relative to uniform_binary^V with every edge parameter J_e in[-log2,0]. This is an explicit existing theorem dependency, not a new assumption or an invocation of arbitrary-alphabet Sidorenko. Since n=6 and m=8, the normalized Gibbs formula gives tau_B(x)>=2^(-n-m)=2^-14 for every binary configuration: its exponential weight is at least2^-m and its reference-normalized partition function is at most1.

construction_and_proof.step: 2. Cycle surplus is available before mixing
construction_and_proof.argument: Let tau_0 be all1 with probability1/3 and tau_B on colors{2,3} with probability2/3. Every singleton and edge is exactly kappa and lambda_0. By the exact block identity, D(tau_0||kappa^V)<=m I_0-3H(1/3,2/3), where I_0=D(lambda_0||kappa^2). Let epsilon=1/100 and R=kappa^V, which is uniform on729 actual configurations. Set nu=(99/100)tau_0+(1/100)R. Every edge is lambda_base=(99/100)lambda_0+(1/100)kappa^2, and the global mixture budget gives m I_base-D(nu||R)>=(99/100)3H(1/3,2/3)-8h(1/100).

construction_and_proof.step: 3. An explicit full-table correction, not separate quotient fitting
construction_and_proof.argument: Define psi(1)=1,psi(2)=-1,psi(3)=0, g(x,y)=Dxy/(kappa_x kappa_y)=-psi(x)psi(y)/600. Define the actual joint law tau(x_V)=nu(x_V)+R(x_V) sum_{uv in E(G)}g(x_u,x_v). For a distinct edge uv, marginalizing a correction from any other edge yields zero: a disjoint edge has mean zero, and an incident but different edge has a centered endpoint because sum_y kappa_y g(x,y)=0. The direct edge term contributes exactly Dxy. Likewise every singleton correction and the total correction vanish. Therefore all original singletons stay kappa and every actual edge becomes lambda_base+D, exactly the displayed target lambda. No quotient-indicator entropy budget is imposed.

construction_and_proof.step: 4. Probability nonnegativity is checked on every actual configuration
construction_and_proof.argument: If a configuration contains color1 and at least one other color, the vertex cut between its color1 set and its complement has at least2 edges. Each edge contributes at most1 to sum psi(x_u)psi(x_v), and every cut edge contributes0 or-1 instead of1. Thus the sum is at most8-2=6, and the correction is at least-R/100; nu>=R/100 pays it. The cut bound holds because G is connected and bridgeless: every edge lies on a4-cycle in K3,3-minus-edge. If the configuration contains no color1, then nu>=(99/100)(2/3)2^-14+R/100. Its correction is at least-(8/600)R, and (99/100)(2/3)2^-14=33/819200>1/218700=R(8/600-1/100). If all colors are1, nu>=(99/100)/3 pays the correction since (99/100)/3>(8/600)R. These three disjoint classes exhaust all configurations. Consequently tau>=0 everywhere, and the already proved normalization makes it an actual probability. Some mixed configurations can have zero mass; the target does not require full joint support.

construction_and_proof.step: 5. Exact total-variation control of the correction
construction_and_proof.argument: The pair correction has total variation delta_P=(1/2)sum_xy|Dxy|=1/2700. The actual joint correction has delta_V=(1/2)sum_x|tau(x)-nu(x)|<=(m/2)E_{kappa^2}|g|=(m/2)sum_xy|Dxy|=2/675. These are rigorous upper bounds from the finite signed construction, not simulation estimates.

construction_and_proof.step: 6. Entropy continuity is paid from the global surplus
construction_and_proof.argument: For probability laws on N points with total variation delta<=1-1/N, maximal coupling gives |H(P)-H(Q)|<=h(delta)+delta log(N-1): condition on disagreement, where each variable has at mostN-1 alternatives given the other. For the uniform references here, D(P||uniform)=logN-H(P), so the same bound controls changes in KL. The right side increases over the stated interval. Apply it with N=9 and delta_P=1/2700 to lambda versus lambda_base, and with N=729 and delta_V<=2/675 to tau versus nu. Thus mI(lambda)-D(tau||R)>=(99/100)3H(1/3,2/3)-8h(1/100)-8[delta_P log8+h(delta_P)]-[delta_V log728+h(delta_V)].

construction_and_proof.step: 7. The resulting budget is strictly positive by elementary rational bounds
construction_and_proof.argument: Use H(1/3,2/3)>log(3/2)>1/3 and h(t)<=t log(1/t)+t. The elementary Taylor bound e>8/3 gives log100<5,log8<3,log2700<9,log728<8 and log(675/2)<7. Therefore8h(1/100)<48/100;8[delta_P log8+h(delta_P)]<104/2700;delta_V log728+h(delta_V)<32/675. The displayed lower bound is strictly greater than99/100-48/100-104/2700-32/675=229/540>2/5. Hence tau is an exact requested witness for the displayed table and actual graph with more than0.4 nats of KL-budget slack. Numerical evaluations of logarithms are unnecessary.
